text:
alana: quick design check — did a small usability pass on the side rail anchors this morning. Two behavioral things popped up: 1) deep-link -> target content gets focus but the left rail item doesn’t show focus/aria state, so keyboard users lose orientation; 2) cluster headers on mobile have touch targets under 44px in a few breakpoints. mike: can you paste steps to repro? alana: repro: 1) open Console -> Models > Versions > Deployments 2) copy a deep link to a deployment detail 3) open in new tab 4) press Tab a few times. Focus lands on the page header but the rail item stays visually unmarked. Breadcrumb also sometimes stays stale when fallback routing runs. sara: is this the same as the old "rail squeeze" issue or a separate affordance problem? @alana alana: related but narrower. Rail squeeze is layout; this is the focus/aria anchor affordance + breadcrumb sync. tom: my quick thoughts — we can approach this 3 ways: A) Programmatically focus the ancestor rail item + add .focus-visible styles and aria-current update. B) Show a transient banner/breadcrumb that points to the rail ("Showing X — reveal in left nav") with a button to reveal. C) Always expand and reveal the full path for any deep-link so the active leaf is visible. Pros/cons: A is light and helps keyboard, C is best for discoverability (esp mobile), B is discoverability-focused but might be noisy. jess: I like A for keyboard users. C helps discoverability for non-keyboard users but could be heavy if deep-links are common. B sounds like an experiment candidate. sara: accessibility nit: when we move focus programmatically make sure the item has role="link" (or button depending on implementation) and aria-current="page" so screen readers get context. Also ensure we respect reduced-motion when animating expand. And add a visible focus indicator, not only color. mike: +1 aria-current. Also we should avoid scrolling the main viewport awkwardly when focusing the rail — use focus options or scroll containment. alana: quick snippet for option A I sketched in fiddle: ```html
  • Deployments
    • ``` tom: tiny worry: focusing the element may cause the rail to auto-scroll and hide main content on smaller screens. Consider `focus({preventScroll:true})` then call container.scrollIntoView if needed, or use `element.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'})`. jess: mobile touch-target: let's bump cluster header hit area to 48px and keep visual compactness by increasing padding rather than height. Also prefer hit-test area separate from visible bounds where feasible. sara: voiceover announcement suggestion: use an aria-live region to announce "Navigated to Deployments — left nav expanded" so assistive tech users know the rail state changed. alana: consensus proposal: implement A as baseline (programmatic focus + aria-current + visible focus styles), respect reduced-motion, and increase mobile hit targets to 48px. Simultaneously ship B as a 10% ephemeral experiment to see if discoverability improves for non-keyboard users (banner with "Reveal in left nav" CTA). Rollout plan: feature-flag experiment -> collect metrics (click on reveal, subsequent navigation, session time). mike: can we add unit tests to assert aria-current gets set and an e2e that simulates deep-link focus restore? jess: I’ll update the style tokens and spacing vars. Will also add a small a11y test for focus indicator contrast. sara: filed an issue: #4382 with summary + acceptance criteria (aria-current, live region message, touch target bump, reduced-motion). design-bot: Comment added on Figma at https://www.figma.com/file/xxx/rail-anchor-proposals — @alana left a note. alana: thanks all — I’ll open the PR and tag @eng-runtime for potential scroll containment/overflow edgecases. If anyone objects to the plan, speak now, otherwise I’ll move forward. :thumbsup:
